name: walk-the-dog
title: Walk the dog, ship the feature
part: What it costs, and how it was built
kicker: How this was built · back to the dog
html:
Walk the dog, ship the feature

Back to the dog. Built a few sentences at a time, one thumb free.

  • Claude Code’s /remote-control on the phone, a personal Max account at home.
  • Test first, every change: Gherkin, a red run, the code, a green run, a gated commit.
  • Evidence, not trust: the gates log every step, so what passed is on record when I get home.
  • The result: repeatable, reliable RISE behaviour, built on walks.

hooks.json

Code reviews by the dog: 0

Prompts shortened by the dog: all of them.

What I couldn’t watch, the gates did: red, green, gated commit, logged.
say: Back to the dog, as promised at the start. Everything you've seen was built a few sentences at a time, by thumb, through Claude Code's /remote-control, on a personal Max account at home. What made that safe wasn't my attention; I was holding a leash. It was a test-first discipline: Gherkin, a red run, the code, a green run, a gated commit, every change. The gates log every step, so what passed is on record when I get home. The humor is real: the messages really were that short. The dog has not reviewed a single pull request, and is still the reason they were short.

deck:ref.label: NO-TIME
deck:ref.title: No time to type
deck:ref.summary: Family and a new dog took the typing time: one hand on a leash, one thumb on a phone. Most of my work is steered that way, through Claude Code's /remote-control, away from the keyboard. So the agents have to act safely while nobody watches every step, and cheaply when they do the same thing again. Hypermedia gives the first (only what the state allows is offered); kept scripts give the second (zero tokens to replay).
